title: Expose deep classifier review and steering through shared Papyrus controls
description:
PLANNING ONLY. Ryan requested filing and design before implementation. This issue is not authorization to build runtime features, deploy, change cloud permissions, publish packages, push, or migrate production data. Keep open pending design review and separate implementation authorization.

As a publication editor, I want real shared Cyclotron controls for labels, explanations, monitoring and steering, so that I can understand and improve the bound classifier in either mode.

Feature: Shared operator experience
  Scenario Outline: Inspect and steer a bound output
    Given an authorized editor using <mode> mode and a selected publication output
    When the editor opens its Cyclotron controls in Papyrus
    Then the UI exposes decision history and explicit human labels with explanations
    And it exposes versioned classifier status, calibration, review routing and learning activity
    And steering actions show their target output, effect and resulting audit history
    And unmeasured metrics and unavailable data are identified honestly
    Examples:
      | mode     |
      | remote   |
      | embedded |
  Scenario: Preserve optional priming
    Given no curated examples have been imported
    When the editor uses the publication
    Then priming is offered optionally and does not block normal operation

Design review / future Definition of Done: review these observable acceptance cases with the shared contract; executable specs and implementation are future work after authorization.
Reuse existing labeling-review/review-control, cyclotron-status, classifier metrics, timeline and inspectable steering components. This story covers missing integration/contract depth, not rewriting completed components. Retain transformation feedback separately from human classification rationale.

Preserve optional curated-example priming (decision-flywheel-da886c09-7acb-45d3-acf8-c81585f26d8a), its preview/revision/explicit-label acceptance contract, and separate existing scholarly research-paper and web-summary transformations. Priming must never become an onboarding gate. Common input items are distinct from publication-specific decisions; one publication accepting an item must never implicitly label another output.
